stories.headline: Apple Signs Tiny Corp Driver Enabling NVIDIA and AMD eGPUs for AI on Apple Silicon Macs

key_facts.fact: Apple officially signed Tiny Corp's TinyGPU driver enabling AMD RDNA3+ and NVIDIA Ampere+ eGPUs to work on Apple Silicon Macs via Thunderbolt 3+ or USB4 ports
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has made one small change that will be hugely beneficial to AI researchers, with a third-party eGPU driver for AI research being signed by Apple

key_facts.fact: The driver is specifically designed for LLM and AI workloads, not gaming or general-purpose graphics acceleration
key_facts.excerpt: Apple approves drivers that let AMD and Nvidia eGPUs run on Mac — software designed for AI, though, and not built for gaming

key_facts.fact: Apple's signing means developers no longer need to disable System Integrity Protection (SIP) to use external GPUs, a major security improvement over previous workarounds
key_facts.excerpt: The approval means that developers can use the driver without needing to disable Apple's System Integrity Protection (SIP) beforehand

key_facts.fact: Tiny Corp, led by George Hotz, developed the driver; it requires macOS 12.1+ and supports AMD RDNA3+ or NVIDIA Ampere+ GPUs
key_facts.excerpt: If you have a Thunderbolt or USB4 eGPU and a Mac, today is the day you've been waiting for! Apple finally approved our driver for both AMD and NVIDIA

stories.headline: Study Finds Most AI Users Exhibit 'Cognitive Surrender,' Accepting Faulty LLM Outputs

key_facts.fact: Research across 1,372 participants and more than 9,000 trials found that most subjects had minimal AI skepticism and accepted faulty AI-generated reasoning without scrutiny
key_facts.excerpt: Research across 1,372 participants and 9K+ trials details 'cognitive surrender,' where most subjects had minimal AI skepticism and accepted faulty AI reasoning

key_facts.fact: In controlled scenarios where researchers deliberately introduced factual errors into AI outputs, 68% of participants failed to identify the mistakes before incorporating them into their work
key_facts.excerpt: In controlled scenarios where researchers deliberately introduced factual errors into AI outputs, 68% of participants failed to identify the mistakes

key_facts.fact: Workers who routinely delegated analytical tasks to language models showed measurable declines in domain-specific reasoning capabilities over the study period
key_facts.excerpt: Workers who routinely delegated analytical tasks to language models showed measurable declines in domain-specific reasoning capabilities over the study period

key_facts.fact: Nearly two-thirds of AI chatbot users exhibit high cognitive offloading, accepting outputs without verification even when they suspect errors
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly two-thirds of AI chatbot users exhibit high cognitive offloading, accepting outputs without verification — even when they suspect errors

key_facts.fact: Researchers noted cognitive surrender is not inherently irrational, as a statistically superior system could plausibly give better-than-human results in probabilistic settings and risk assessment
key_facts.excerpt: Cognitive surrender is not inherently irrational... a statistically superior system could plausibly give better-than-human results in domains such as probabilistic settings, risk assessment, or extensive data

sources.title: Research finds AI users scarily willing to surrender their cognition to LLMs

stories.headline: Microsoft Copilot Terms of Use Classify It as 'Entertainment Purposes Only,' Contradicting Marketing

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's Copilot Terms of Use, updated in October 2025, state under bold capital letters 'IMPORTANT DISCLOSURES & WARNINGS' that 'Copilot is for entertainment purposes only'
key_facts.excerpt: According to Microsoft Copilot Terms of Use, updated in Oct. 2025, 'Copilot is for entertainment purposes only' and 'Don't rely on Copilot for important advice'

key_facts.fact: The terms warn users not to rely on Copilot for important advice, to use it at their own risk, and that Microsoft makes no warranty about the tool's responses
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft's Copilot terms of service explicitly state that the product is intended solely for entertainment purposes... Copilot can make mistakes

key_facts.fact: The disclaimer contradicts Microsoft's aggressive enterprise marketing positioning Copilot as a productivity tool, with AI researcher Gary Marcus commenting 'Imagine if calculators had to carry this warning'
key_facts.excerpt: These might be boilerplate disclaimers, but they kind of contradict the company's ads and marketing

key_facts.fact: Microsoft also disclaims that Copilot's responses may infringe copyrights, trademarks, or rights of privacy, and users are solely responsible for any shared outputs
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft cannot promise that Copilot's responses won't infringe someone else's rights like copyrights, trademarks, or rights of privacy

key_facts.excerpt: There are more than 67,000 open software engineering roles at tech companies, up about 30% so far this year

key_facts.fact: Software engineering listings have climbed approximately 30% since the start of 2026 and are up roughly 2x since mid-2023
key_facts.excerpt: Open software engineering roles at tech companies are up about 30% so far this year

key_facts.fact: TrueUp founder Amit Taylor said much of the narrative around AI replacing engineers is not grounded in job posting data, with AI-related roles specifically 'exploding'
key_facts.excerpt: Much of the narrative around AI replacing engineers simply is not grounded in job posting data, at least not yet. AI-related roles specifically are what he described as exploding

stories.headline: Y Combinator Parts Ways With AI Compliance Startup Delve Over Fabricated Cert Allegations

key_facts.fact: Y Combinator removed AI compliance startup Delve from its portfolio directory on April 4, a rare move from the accelerator which has backed over 4,000 companies
key_facts.excerpt: The compliance startup Delve has ended its relationship with accelerator Y Combinator, apparently as a consequence of surrounding controversy

key_facts.fact: Anonymous whistleblower posts by 'DeepDelver' alleged Delve fabricated SOC 2 compliance certifications for hundreds of clients using auto-generated reports
key_facts.excerpt: Delve misled clients about their privacy and security compliance status, auto-generated reports, and relied on low-quality certification providers who approved reports without proper scrutiny

key_facts.fact: Delve co-founder Selin Kocalar confirmed the split on X, saying 'YC and Delve have parted ways,' while co-founder Karun Kaushik characterized the allegations as a smear campaign
key_facts.excerpt: Delve co-founder Selin Kocalar posted on X that 'YC and Delve have parted ways'

key_facts.fact: Allegations also included that Delve took an open-source tool and passed it off as proprietary work without proper license attribution
key_facts.excerpt: DeepDelver claimed that Delve allegedly took an open source tool and passed it off as its own work without proper license attribution
